A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProLong study. Their main text, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and matchable, including the expanded Appendix B in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original training and SFT ablations, ProLong benchmark results, and implementation-throughput measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds generator-quality experiments, post-SFT short-context evaluations, and additional benchmark results.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains Llama-3 initialization, staged 64K/512K continued training, RoPE scaling, document masking, and UltraChat SFT. The stronger synthetic-data generator is an experimental variant; no new component is adopted for ProLong. The revised data proportions are reported settings changes.

E1.justification: Final evaluation expands from the HELMET development subset to all available HELMET tasks, visibly adding Cite in Table 10. Table 26 adds RULER and ∞Bench evaluations, including additional calculation and retrieval subtasks. NoCha and the existing short-context datasets remain.

E2.justification: The main Table 10 comparator set is retained. V2 adds GPT-4o-mini in Table 26 and a Llama-3-8B-Instruct plus UltraChat control in Table 25. Table 24 directly compares ProLong's data mixture with the already evaluated Fu et al. strategy.

E3.justification: Table 10 changes from averaging 32K, 64K, and 128K results to reporting 128K only, with expanded task coverage and Cite included in the average. Added evaluations include post-SFT short-context controls and a 70B synthetic-data generator. Table 9 revises Wikipedia from 8% to 11% and Tulu-v2 from 11% to 8% within ShortMix; this does not establish that ProLong was retrained.

E4.justification: V2 adds ArXiv and Books/Repos/ArXiv mixture ablations in Table 4, tests whether synthetic-SFT findings persist with a stronger generator in B.5, and adds controlled data-mixture and post-SFT retention analyses in B.6–B.7. Conversely, Figure 2 loses its Recall, ICL, QA, and summarization training trajectories.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over two training runs in Figure 2. V2 retains that practice for the remaining panels and introduces no new run-count disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 10 replaces the main results: ProLong's average is 60.2 under v1's summary and 49.4 under v2's expanded 128K evaluation, which is not a same-setting decline. New results include a best 70B-generated SFT mixture average of 55.4 versus 55.7 for short-only SFT, post-SFT short-context average 69.4, and RULER/∞Bench scores of 71.9/48.0. NoCha and Table 11 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4 adds a simplified mathematical dependency-count argument under explicit assumptions about distance-specific learning and uniform dependency positions. It claims that one length-nd document supplies (n−1)(d−1) more distance-d dependencies than n length-d documents. This limited mathematical addition is qualified as an unrealistic idealization; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: downstream evaluation after SFT, carefully mixed long and short data, benefits from longer training sequences, effective short-only SFT, and ProLong's 40B-token training and 512K context window. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds a dependency-span explanation for longer-sequence training. Appendix B.7 acknowledges post-SFT MMLU/GSM8K deficits and hypothesizes an effect from unavailable instruction data; B.8 attributes counterintuitive benchmark rankings to narrow coverage and noisy metrics. Existing resource and model-scale limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table 9 revises the documented Wikipedia/Tulu-v2 proportions. New appendix passages specify the 70B generator and UltraChat control construction and explicitly document matched settings for the Fu comparison. Existing hardware, training-stack, processing, prompt-template, and resource-access disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works remain the same; HELMET's update to its 2025 ICLR entry is bibliographic. Positioning is modestly expanded through the explicit comparison with Fu et al.'s data strategy in B.6 and criticism of RULER/∞Bench coverage and metric reliability in B.8.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order remain intact. V2 makes localized abstract and introduction edits, revises Section 2 headings, adds explanatory passages and cross-references, and extends Appendix B with subsections B.5–B.8.

P2.justification: The visual evidence is substantially expanded and revised: Figure 2 changes from six panels to two inset panels, Table 4 gains ablation rows, Table 10 gains Cite and a revised caption, and Tables 23–26 present additional analyses and benchmarks. The original QA examples are retained as Table 27, not newly added.

improvement.justification: V1 already provides extensive ablations and NoCha validation. V2 strengthens that evidence with held-out HELMET tasks, additional benchmarks, a stronger-generator check, and post-SFT retention controls. These gains outweigh limited losses from removing four Figure 2 panels and leaving inaccurate Section 6.2 prose: Table 10 now shows ProLong ahead of Llama-3.1-8B on summarization but behind on Cite. The net improvement is in validation, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.
